props.title: A funk band for parties, after-parties and patios.

The client strip, sitewide. Directly under the intro so the names land on the
     first screen.

props.title: James Brown to Prince, played as instrumentals.
props.lede: James Brown, the Meters, Stevie Wonder, Herbie Hancock, Sly and the Family Stone, Prince, Earth, Wind & Fire and the funk side of Motown. Your guests know these records by the bass line and the horn parts, and that’s what the band plays.

props.html: While people eat, the band plays the slower, warmer end of the book, and the tempos come up once the floor opens. When you want the same songwriters sung, the soul and R&B band is this band with a singer out front. The rest of the covers list is on the repertoire page.

props.title: A trio, or a quartet with a horn or keys.

rows.text: Guitar, bass and drums. It’s the size for a floor that sits close to the tables: a club dining space, a restaurant buyout, a backyard with a patio.

The trio plus a horn or keys, for a ballroom or a crowd past two hundred, where three musicians start to sound thin across a wide floor. A horn plays the lines the records gave it, and keys fill in under the guitar solos.

props.html: A jazz duo or a solo guitarist can play the drinks hour before the band on the same contract, and the DJ can keep the party going afterward through the same sound system.

rows.text: A fortieth or a fiftieth at a club, a restaurant or the house. The trio fills a floor without a stage, which is why it’s the size most of these parties book.

The hour after a company dinner or a conference program, played on the sound system that’s already set up for the evening. It books like the rest of a company event, on one contract with the paperwork your office needs.
A lawn or a rooftop in July. Instrumental funk works from anywhere on the lawn, so people can dance near the band or keep eating at the far tables.

rows.term: The last night of a retreat
rows.text: The one night the whole company is in one place with the agenda finished, at a mountain venue or back in Denver.

props.html: Stage sizes and power for each size are on the technical page, and the questions every booking shares, from substitutions to volume limits, are on the full question list.

items.a: An instrumental funk and soul band booked through Signet Artists in Denver: guitar, bass and drums as a trio, or a quartet with a horn or keys, playing James Brown, the Meters, Stevie Wonder, Prince and Earth, Wind & Fire for parties, company after-parties and summer events.

No, it's an instrumental band, so the songs can run into each other for as long as the floor wants. The soul and R&B band plays the same songwriters with a singer out front and a horn on the choruses.

While people eat, it plays at a level the tables talk across, with the drums kept light. Once the floor opens it plays like a band at a party, with the bass felt at the back of the floor and the guitar kept comfortable for the front tables. It sets the level to the space and the crowd, and if your venue has a sound limit, give us the number and it stays under it.

items.q: How much space and power does it need?
items.a: The trio sets up in about 12 by 8 feet on one dedicated 20-amp circuit and needs about an hour to set up. The quartet takes about 14 by 10 feet, two dedicated circuits and 90 minutes. Sound support that's the right size for the venue comes with every booking.

Yes, and patios and lawns are a lot of its work. It needs a covered, level and dry spot with power run to it, and we agree a plan for moving indoors with you ahead of time, because a Colorado afternoon can turn fast.

items.q: Can we add time or ask for a song?
items.a: Yes. If the night runs long, another half hour is easy to add on the night, and the band learns one song of your choosing as part of every booking.

props.title: Send us the date, and the funk band brings the floor.
props.lede: Live music for your event, from a solo musician to a full band, with sound support that’s the right size for the venue and a personal contact for the night.
